summary: SWAT background-resilience patch — source-level verification (no web preview possible: expo-sqlite wasm-worker bundling failure is a known/documented limitation; SwatBus native foreground service is APK-only). Verified: (a) swatIrc.ts reconnect logic — onclose while wantConnected schedules Math.min(60000, 1000*2**attempts), increments attempts, sets status 'connecting'; onclose while !wantConnected sets 'down'; IRC 001 resets attempts=0 and sets 'connected'; disconnectSwat cancels reconnectTimer, resets attempts=0, calls busStop, sets 'down'. (b) swatBus.ts wrapper — HAS_SWAT_BUS = Platform.OS==='android' && !!NativeModules.SwatBus (false on web/expo-go); busStart/busStop/busUpdate/busEnableKeepAlive all guard on HAS_SWAT_BUS and wrap N.* in try/catch → safe no-ops when NativeModule absent. (c) SwatTab.tsx AppState 'active' handler kicks connectSwat if intended-connected & status is 'down' — matches spec. (d) parseIrcColored/stripIrc unchanged and pass all 9 palette/segmentation tests; backoff formula verified across 9 attempt values (0→1s, 6+→60s cap). (e) TypeScript compile of swatIrc.ts + swatBus.ts is clean (tsc --noEmit); project-wide tsc has only 2 pre-existing errors in MCPTab.tsx unrelated to this patch. (f) app.json registers withSwatBus config plugin; Kotlin module/package/service files present.

Live/runtime verification (foreground service, wakelock, actual reconnect timing, notification permission dialog, battery-opt exemption) requires a real APK build on Android; cannot be validated here.
Unrelated pre-existing tsc errors in src/components/MCPTab.tsx:856,871 ('execChroot' used before declaration) — NOT introduced by this patch, but worth cleaning up in a future pass.
critical_code_review_comments: swatIrc.ts:78-84 — emit() reassigns `state = snap` inside listeners.forEach. Since snap is captured before the loop and each listener may call set() (which mutates state), this pattern effectively rewinds state to the pre-listener snapshot between listeners. Pre-existing, not from this patch, but worth flagging.

swatIrc.ts:329-341 — sock.onclose does not guard the reconnect scheduling with `if (ws === sock)`. If connectSwat() is called again before an old socket's onclose fires, the stale close handler will still schedule another reconnect and stomp status back to 'connecting'. Low-impact because the very-next connectSwat clears reconnectTimer, but a strict identity check would be more defensive.

swatIrc.ts:334 — attempts is a module-level counter; after a manual disconnectSwat() → connectSwat() cycle it's reset to 0 (good). But a rapid succession of connect() calls without a full disconnect could leak attempts across sessions. Minor.
swatBus.ts — try/catch swallows all errors silently. Acceptable for a bridge wrapper, but at least a __DEV__ console.warn would help debug native bridge misconfigurations.

rca_of_issue: Original bug: backgrounding the app killed the SWAT IRC WebSocket because JS timers/sockets are suspended when the Android host process is backgrounded and there was no reconnect path when it resumed. Fix implemented: (1) exponential-backoff auto-reconnect (1s→60s) in sock.onclose while wantConnected=true (swatIrc.ts:329-341); (2) attempts=0 reset on IRC 001 (swatIrc.ts:247); (3) AppState 'active' listener in SwatTab.tsx kicks connectSwat immediately if status==='down' & autoconnect (SwatTab.tsx:60-65); (4) native SwatBusService (Android foreground service + PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK + persistent notification) to keep the JS runtime alive in background (APK-only, no-op elsewhere); (5) opt-in busEnableKeepAlive() requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS + battery-optimisation exemption. Reproduction requires a real device backgrounded for >30s; cannot be reproduced or fully validated in this container.
